heading: EXT. LAKE - DIVING PLATFORM - LATE AFTERNOON, END OF SUMMER

units.text: EXT. LAKE - DIVING PLATFORM - LATE AFTERNOON, END OF SUMMER
A wooden platform floats on oil drums, sun-bleached and splintered, anchored fifty yards from shore.
Beyond, pines darken the hills.
Water slaps the barrels in a slow rhythm.
The light is amber, the air already cooler.
LEILANI KAMAKA (17, wet hair, towel around her shoulders, a paperback damp at the corners) sits on the edge with her feet in the water.
JONAH FELDSTEIN (17, sunburned nose, swim trunks faded to grey) lies flat on his back, staring at the sky.
CRICKET OYELARAN-PARK (16, skinny, goggles pushed up, a wristwatch that is too big) sits cross-legged between them, building a tiny stack of pebbles.
A radio somewhere on shore plays a song that was popular in June.
Fifteen days.
units.name: CRICKET

units.text: Don't.
units.name: JONAH

units.text: Until school.
units.name: CRICKET

units.text: He said don't.
units.name: LEILANI

units.text: I'm only saying it out loud so it's less scary.
units.name: CRICKET

units.text: It's not less scary.
units.name: JONAH

units.text: No. It's not.
units.name: CRICKET

units.text: Silence.
A loon cries across the lake.
Leilani lifts her feet from the water and hugs her knees.
The sun sinks another inch.
Their shadows stretch across the planks, three long fingers pointing at nothing.
I won't be on the bus.
units.name: LEILANI

units.text: Jonah props up on one elbow.
What?
units.name: JONAH

units.text: My mom got the job in Tacoma. We leave Friday.
units.name: LEILANI

units.text: Friday.
units.name: JONAH

units.text: This Friday?
units.name: CRICKET

units.text: I was going to tell you.
units.name: LEILANI

units.text: Cricket knocks over the pebble stack.
It makes no sound on the wet wood.
Okay.
units.name: JONAH

units.text: Okay?
units.name: LEILANI

units.text: What do you want me to say?
units.name: JONAH

units.text: I don't know. Something.
units.name: LEILANI

units.text: Jonah sits up, brushes sand from his palms.
He looks at the shore, where the dock lights are coming on one by one.
You'll hate it there.
units.name: JONAH

units.text: Probably.
units.name: LEILANI

units.text: Good.
units.name: JONAH

units.text: She laughs, wet and short.
Cricket pulls his goggles down over his eyes like a mask and lies back.
Can we stay here until the sun is gone?
units.name: CRICKET

units.text: Yeah.
units.name: LEILANI

units.text: Yeah.
units.name: JONAH

units.text: They lie shoulder to shoulder on the platform.
The light fades from gold to rose to a deep, cool blue.
The barrels creak beneath them.
On shore, someone turns off the radio.
Leilani reaches across Cricket and takes Jonah's hand.
He doesn't look at her.
He holds on.
Stars come out, one at a time.
